note: Each clip is one TTS call. A phrase is one caption cue: `show` is the caption text, `say` (if different) is what the voice reads.

phrases.show: This is a graphics card.
Most of the time, a lot of its memory sits unused.
Meanwhile, developers want open models
without renting and running a server.
Moonlight connects the two.
Earn from your spare GPU.
Use open models for less.
Sellers run one small agent.
It finds the open models they already have,
in Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM,
phrases.say: in Ollama, LM Studio, llama dot C P P, or V L L M,

phrases.show: and serves them in the VRAM their own apps aren't using.
phrases.say: and serves them in the V-RAM their own apps aren't using.

phrases.show: Buyers get one OpenAI-compatible API,
and pay only for the tokens they use.
Here's a seller joining.
One line installs the agent.
Run moonlight.
It lists the models on this machine
and prints a pairing code.
Approve the computer in the browser, and you're selling.
No keys to copy, no ports to open.
The terminal becomes a live dashboard:
each model's status, jobs served, earnings,
and how the GPU memory splits
between your apps, Moonlight, and what's spare.
And when your own apps need the GPU,
Moonlight pauses, finishes what it's doing, and steps aside.
On the web, the same computer shows its VRAM bar and earnings.
phrases.say: On the web, the same computer shows its V-RAM bar and earnings.

phrases.show: Sellers keep 90% of every request,
phrases.say: Sellers keep ninety percent of every request,

phrases.show: at the price they set.
Now the buyer.
In Chat, pick “Any small model” and ask anything.
phrases.say: In Chat, pick “Any small model,” and ask anything.

phrases.show: The answer streams from a seller's GPU,
and the receipt shows which GPU served it,
what it cost, and that it's verified.
For your own code, create an API key.
Point the OpenAI SDK at Moonlight's base URL,
and that's the whole integration.
Or let Moonlight pick:
auto/chat-small routes to the best available GPU.
phrases.say: auto slash chat small routes to the best available GPU.

phrases.show: But how do you know a seller runs the model they listed?
Moonlight hides canary jobs among real requests.
At eight points in a reference answer,
the seller's next three words have to match
what a trusted reference GPU says.
This seller lists Qwen 2.5 1.5B
phrases.say: This seller lists Qwen two point five, one point five B,

phrases.show: but secretly serves the 0.5B.
phrases.say: but secretly serves the zero point five B.

phrases.show: A few checks later, it's flagged,
taken off the market, and its earnings are held.
Moonlight.
Earn from your spare GPU.
Use open models for less.
